summary: Drove mypintusan's SCREENS for the first time (tools/fleetbench/bench_pintusan_screens.py + uicheck_pintusan.js/_partb/_partc, 166 checks over six headless-Chrome passes: every section in all four languages including RTL Arabic, admin workflows confirmed against the server, and the operator and viewer roles compared control-by-control against what the matrix would actually allow). Item 6 of the hardening register for the app that physically opens doors, and the last app in the suite with zero screen coverage after six API benches. FIVE DEFECTS, four of them making the non-admin half of the product unusable, plus one nobody could have found without looking at a picture. (1) THE OPERATOR ROLE'S ONE POWER DID NOT EXIST. services/rbac.go argues at length that opening a door remotely is an operator power - 'what a receptionist does all day' - and wrote the rule as '/api/doors/unlock'. The route is /api/doors/{id}/unlock. The matcher is segment-wise, so a three-segment rule can never match a four-segment request; the most specific rule that DID match was '/api/doors', which is read-only, so every remote open by an operator was refused on every install. (2) THE SESSION PROBE WAS NOT IN THE CATALOG, so it was denied by default: a viewer or operator signed in successfully - /api/auth/login is public and answered 200 - and GET /api/auth/session was then refused, `user` stayed null, and the SPA rendered the sign-in card again. Correct credentials, no error, straight back to the login screen, forever, while every endpoint the catalog grants them answered 200 to a direct request. (3) THE HOME SCREEN WAS AN ERROR PAGE FOR EVERY NON-ADMIN. Doors.js loaded the door list and the lockdown state in one Promise.all, and lockdown was admin-only, so a refused read did not hide a pill - it rejected the whole load and rendered 'you do not have permission for this action' where the doors should be. The two loads now settle independently, and SEEING that the site is sealed is now granted separately from sealing it: an operator who cannot see a lockdown cannot explain why nothing is opening, which is the exact minute they most need the screen. (4) `write` GRANTS POST AND NOTHING ELSE. '/api/holders' was Operator: write, so an operator could enrol a person and got 403 on the list - the first call the People screen makes. Now readWrite, with the trap named on the constant. (5) THE ROLES WERE UNASSIGNABLE. EnsureRoles seeds viewer, operator and admin on every boot and NOTHING served a route that could put a person in one, so an appliance had exactly one account and every distinction the catalog draws was theoretical: new apis/users.go (roles + user CRUD + password reset, on the shared appliance user service so bcrypt, sessions and the last-administrator guard stay one implementation) and a Users section on the Settings screen. ROOT CAUSE OF THE SCREEN HALF, fixed rather than patched: this app decided authorization TWICE - the server with the deny-by-default matrix, the SPA with a client-side user.isAdmin - and the two drifted in BOTH directions at once (a viewer was offered an Unlock button on every door card and an 'Add person' button; an operator granted read on grants and schedules had the entire Access rules section hidden). New apis/capabilities.go answers GET /api/auth/capabilities by calling Authorize on the REAL route each control would send, and App.js, Doors.js, People.js, Access.js, Readers.js and Settings.js all render from it, so an offer on screen cannot disagree with a decision on the server and the screens follow the catalog when it changes. AND THE ONE THE ASSERTIONS COULD NEVER SEE: opening the screenshots showed every table on every screen rendering RAW WHITE BROWSER BUTTONS labelled 'Sort' jammed under each column heading, in all four languages, on every install - @shared/DataTable ships markup and no style ('styled by the consuming app's stylesheet', its own header says) and mypintusan was the only app in the suite that used it and never wrote them. Ported from rbac-standard.css and rebound to this app's warm palette, with the pager arrows mirrored for Arabic. Every check passed while that was on screen: the screens rendered, every control was hit-testable, no dictionary key leaked, the API answered correctly. ALSO FIXED: the Readers screen computed its Security column from the admin-only access settings and swallowed the refusal, so a non-admin saw 'Not encrypted' against readers running encrypted sessions - a confident wrong answer about the security of a door, on the screen that exists to answer exactly that; it now says 'Not shown' and says why. The Access rules screen renders read-only for an operator, with a line explaining it, rather than offering edits the server refuses. New services/rbac_test.go is the first test this catalog has ever had - it seeds the REAL catalog through the REAL permission service and asserts every rule governs a route the app serves AND every route is covered by a rule, in both directions, which is what would have caught (1) and (2) at build time. domain/shared/services.PathGoverns exports the matcher so any app's catalog can be tested the same way. 166/166 checks pass with the fixes; 91/96 against the unfixed app, where the whole operator and viewer half was unreachable and therefore unmeasurable.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema change, no config change, no breaking API change. New endpoints: GET /api/auth/capabilities (readable by every signed-in role), and GET /api/settings/roles plus /api/settings/users CRUD and /api/settings/users/{id}/password (admin-only, and each guarded a second time in the handler). Permission changes are all WIDENING and all restore intent the catalog already stated: viewer and operator gain GET on /api/auth/session (without which they could not use the UI at all) and on /api/lockdown (seeing the site is sealed; POST stays admin-only), operator gains GET on /api/holders and POST on /api/doors/{id}/unlock. Nothing that was permitted becomes denied. Existing installs pick the new rows up on the next boot: EnsureApplianceRoles BACKFILLS - it adds rows only for catalog paths a role has no row for at all and never touches an existing row's verbs - so a site that has retuned its operator keeps its edits, and the corrected /api/doors/*/unlock rule is a NEW path rather than an edit of the old one. The dead '/api/doors/unlock' row is left behind on such installs and governs nothing, exactly as it always did. Operators and viewers will see screens they have never been able to reach before, which is the point of the work; an administrator sees an unchanged app apart from the new Users section on Settings and correctly styled tables. Scope is `infra` rather than `mypintusan`: mypintusan has no entry in infra/versioning/version.json's apps map yet, and an unknown scope token hard-fails the release run.
